actions.purpose: Eighth-block precision for stacked columns, the no-empty-track rule, and a reset-marked sparkline in the shared kit
actions.prompt:
In /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard change the shared drawing kit src/workflow/dash-kit.js (and its tests in tests/dash-kit.test.js) so the pages built on it can close requirements 4 and 8. Screenshots: [screenshot removed: it showed private project data] and [screenshot removed: it showed private project data]. [owner request, paraphrased] The Trends chart draws a bar above its own value line, lists codex and command-code in the legend while they are invisible in every bar, and spaces tick labels unevenly; the Run page budget block draws a dotted track and a dash for a pool with no meter.

1. `columnBars` (around line 575-680): today each bar's height is `Math.ceil(value / scale * rowCount)` whole cells and each pool slice is whole cells too, so a bar overshoots the axis and a slice under one cell vanishes. Rework it so (a) the axis top and the row count are chosen together from `niceStep` such that every tick value lands exactly on a row and the spacing between tick labels is even (e.g. ≈$3.00 in 6 rows of $0.50, or 9 rows of $0.25 when the height allows), (b) heights are computed in eighths of a row and the top cell of each bar uses the partial glyphs ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█ so a bar never rises above its own value, (c) stacked slices are laid smallest-on-top and every non-zero slice is at least one eighth-block tall, taking that eighth from the largest slice so the total height stays exact, (d) the colour of a partial top glyph is the colour of the slice it belongs to. Keep the existing signature and the click regions per column; callers in src/workflow/dashboard.js (Home spent per day) and src/workflow/stats-view.js (Trends) must keep working unchanged, so if you need a new option make it opt-in with the old behaviour as default only where a test pins it, and say in your report which option the two callers should pass.
2. Add a helper for the no-empty-track rule, e.g. `absentLine(label, reason, {width})` returning a dim one-line row `label   reason` sized to the width, plus a documented convention in a comment at the top of dash-kit.js: a page never draws a dotted or blank track, meter or bar for data it does not have; it writes the reason in words on that row. Also give `shareBar`/`progressBar` a way to render a caller-supplied partial glyph so the Run page can show `≈ 0.4%` as a sliver rather than nothing.
3. Add `sparkline` support for markers: `sparkline(values, width, { markers: [indexes] })` draws `▏` at a marked index (a licence window reset) in place of that day's glyph, keeping the width; Stats Pools will use it with one caption. Document the glyph meaning in the function comment.
4. Tests in tests/dash-kit.test.js: a ≈$2.93 bar on a ≈$3.00 axis ends below the top row (pin the exact glyph rows), tick labels are evenly spaced, a 1-cent slice inside a $3 bar is visible as one eighth-block, `absentLine` fits the width and carries no block glyphs, and `sparkline` with markers places `▏` at the marked index. Run `node --test tests/dash-kit.test.js` and the full suite.

In `budgetWeekLines` (dashboard.js ~line 2110-2160) the phone slices to 3 pools (`slice(0, narrow ? 3 : 4)`) and uses a 9-character name column: show every pool the desktop shows, or end the block with `+N more`, and size the name column to the longest name up to 16 so `claude-code:acme` and `claude-code` differ. In the four-column breakdown band (~line 2304-2375) the phone stacks the lists but draws only the first row and lets the share bar eat the percentage (`24…`): show the top three rows per list (or `+N more`), and size the bar as width minus label minus the percentage text so the percentage is always whole. In `summaryBand` the phone joins two figures per line with ` · `: one figure per line on the phone. Shorten the spent tile's phone empty state so it fits its row (say what the desktop says in fewer words, e.g. `no estimate today`). Pass the new columnBars option so Home's spent-per-day chart is drawn to eighth-block precision.

Requirement 2, keys. `DASHBOARD_KEYS` (line ~142-160) binds `help: keyRow('h/?', 'Help', ['h', '?'])`; the tab table (~1698), the nav row (~1927-1930) and the Help page text refer to `h` as Help. For a finished run that is not in the history index, derive the project the way `workflow reindex` does (find that derivation in the reindex path in src/workflow/cli.js or wherever `rollupRecord(..., { project })` is called, and reuse the same function: the run's goal.json `intent.cwd`, mapped through the same repo/worktree naming so `/home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-handoff` becomes `bullswarm`). `unknown project` remains only when no cwd is recorded. Add a test with a run directory that has goal.json but no rollup.

Requirement 7, Runs and History become one page ([screenshot removed: it showed private project data] is the two-line-per-run list to remove; [screenshot removed: it showed private project data] is the table to keep). `runsPage` (~2689) and `historyPage` (~3382): the Runs page gets an `── active ──` block first, listing every running or waiting run with the same plan strip and per-step bar Home's running section draws (reuse that code, do not fork it), then History's day-grouped table (`historyLines` from history-view.js) with the selection cursor over the rows, so Enter and the digits open a run and the existing lazy loading of older days keeps working. Move the `agents` and `run it` blocks (~2721, ~2744) to the Help page. Remove History from the tab row (tabs: Home, Runs, Budget, Stats, Fleet) and make `y` open Runs scrolled to the first day header. Keep the History page module (history-view.js) as the table renderer; the `history` page id may stay as an alias that renders Runs. Update every test that asserts the tab list or the History tab, and add tests: the active block shows a running run with its bar; a finished run row opens on Enter; `y` lands on a day header; the tab row has five entries at 120 columns and the phone row (55 columns) is Home, Runs, Budget, Stats and fits Fleet if it has room.

Requirement 8, wording on the Run page ([screenshot removed: it showed private project data]). The Run page budget block (find the code that prints the dotted track and the `— no measured %/minute rate for <pool>` footnote, near line ~3036-3070): title it `licence this run used`, print whole percents with one decimal only under 1% (`≈ 0.4% of the weekly plan`), draw an unmetered pool with `absentLine(pool, 'free model · no licence meter')` instead of a track, and when no pool is metered collapse the block to one sentence. In the plan strip's pool row, when the cell cannot fit `pool · model · effort`, show the pool name alone rather than `openc…`. When the run's lifecycle is paused, the live block says `paused · bullswarm workflow resume <shortId> continues it` instead of `waiting for the next dispatch` (line ~3036). Replace the footnote at ~3070 with `ETA —: <step id> has no recorded duration yet` (list the step ids when there are several). Tests for each.

actions.purpose: Budget page rewritten in reader words and Stats Pools with per-row reset-marked sparklines
actions.prompt:
In /home/dev/Repo/bullswork/bullswarm-dashboard you own src/workflow/budget-view.js, src/workflow/budget-model.js, src/workflow/stats-view.js and their tests. Read the chart-kit dependency output first: it names `absentLine`, the `sparkline` markers option and the columnBars precision option you must use. Deliver requirements 5 and 6, and requirement 8's rule on your pages.

Requirement 6, Budget ([screenshot removed: it showed private project data]). Today each pool is seven rows in engine words: a meter with `60% used`, `Resets Mon 21 Sept, 20:00 <local zone> · 46.4% of the window elapsed · on track`, `Subscription rate: —`, a right-aligned `≈ $3.06 API-equivalent estimate 58 median runs still fi` that truncates, a purple share bar captioned `workflows 1.02% · rest 58.98% · 41.77 measured worker-minutes`, and `biggest workflows: dahnys · 114.22 worker-minutes · ≈ $0.43 API-equivalent estimate w6p38i · …`. Grok shows `workflows 131.24% · rest 0% · ≈ workflows exceeds the reported meter`. Rewrite `budgetLines` (budget-view.js:293) and `budgetNotes` (:340), and the strings budget-model.js supplies (:377, :386, :468), so each pool reads: header `claude-code · weekly plan · resets Mon 21 Sept 20:00 (in 2d 18h)`; row `used` = the meter, whole percent, then `46% of the window gone → on track` (or `slow`); row `by bullswarm` = a bar of bullswarm's share of the plan as a whole percent with `(42 min of work)` and `· other tools 59%`; row `room` = `about 58 more medium runs before the reset` (blank with a reason when not computable); row `so far` = `≈ $3.06 of API-equivalent work · biggest: dahnys ≈ $0.43, w6p38i ≈ $0.46`. Whole numbers everywhere (minutes and percents rounded; money keeps cents). The subscription line appears only when a price is declared (`plan · $200/mo declared`), never `Subscription rate: —`. When the measured share exceeds the meter, the `by bullswarm` bar is capped at the meter and one footnote says `bullswarm's own measurement is above what the meter reports; the meter lags`. A pool with no meter (opencode) or no measured rate gets one `absentLine` in words, not a dotted track. The page-foot notes become one short block: what ≈ means, and the `bullswarm strategy set-subscription <pool> --monthly-usd <amount>` hint once. Keep the ≈/basis rules and every real figure; keep the phone form (55 columns) to the same rows with shorter labels; nothing truncates at 170 or 200 columns (measure the right-hand tails).

Requirement 5, Stats Pools ([screenshot removed: it showed private project data]). `stats-view.js:1204` draws a shared `licence used per day, by pool` line chart with no legend, five rows for 0–100%, lines that overlap, and a `▏ reset` legend cut off at the right edge; the per-pool rows below overflow (`≈ $3.06 AP`, `2 runs · ✓ 100`). Remove the shared chart. On each pool row put a seven-day sparkline built with the kit's `sparkline(values, 7, { markers })` from that pool's end-of-day usage series (the same series the chart used; find where it is assembled), with `▏` on a day whose window reset, followed by the live meter, `60% · on track`, and the run figures; measure the row so the tail fits at 170 and 200 columns and use shorter labels at 55. One caption under the block: `each glyph is that day's usage at day end · a drop after ▏ is the window resetting`. Pools with no meter get one `absentLine` (`meter unavailable · N runs`) instead of a dotted track. Pass the columnBars precision option on Trends so its stacked columns follow requirement 4. Keep every existing click region.

Capture Budget and Stats Pools (and Trends) at 55x26, 60x50, 170x35, 200x50 under /tmp/review-budget-pools/.
